div.l: That he vouchesaf so for to doo
And that he wolde be oure gouernour
And of oure tales be Iuge and reportour
And sett a souper at a certain pris
And we will reuled be at his deuys
In high and lowe and thus be oon assent
We ben accorded to his Iugement
And thereupon̄ the wyn was fet anon̄
And dranke and to reste went echon̄
Withoute any lenger tarieng
At morwe whan day began to springe
Vp ros oure oost and was oure alder cok
And gadered vs to gider in a flok
And forth we riden a litill more paas
Vnto the watring of Seint Thomas
And there oure oost began his hors areste
And seid Lordinges herkeneth if you leste
Ye wot youre forward and I it you recorde
If euene song and morwe song acorde
Lat se now who shall telle the first tale
As euer mot I drinke wyn or ale
Who so will be rebell to my Iugement
Shal paie for al that bi the weie is spent
Now draweth cutt or we forther twinne
The wich hath the shortest shal beginne
Sir quod he my master and my Lord
Now draweth cutt for this is my accord
Cometh ner quod he my Lady Prioresse
And ye sir clerk lat be your shamefastnesse
Ne studieth nat lay hond to euerichon̄
Anon̄ to drawe eueri wight began
And shortli for to telle as it was
Were it be auenture or soort or caas
The soth it is the knotte fill to the kniȝt
Of wich full blithe was eueri wiȝt
And telle must his tale as was reson
By forward and be composicion
As ye haue herd what nedeth wordes moo
And whan this good man saugh þᵗat it is so
And he was wise and obedient
To kepe his forward be his fre assent
He seid sithan I shal beginne the game
What welcome be the knotte on goddes name
Now late vs ride and herkne what I sey
And with that word we riden forth oure wey
And he be gan̄ right thus with a goodli cheer
His tale anon and seid as ye may hiere
Hiere beginneth the Kniȝt his tale .
Uhilom as olde stories telle vs

Ther was a Duc that Theseus
Hight ·
Of Athenes he was gouernoᵘur
And in his tyme was such conqueroᵘur
That gretter was ther non vnder sonne
Full many a riche contre had he wonne
That with his wisdam and his chiualrie
He conquered all the reigne of Femynye
That whilom I cleped was Sithia
And wedded the quene Ipolita
And brouȝt hir hom with him in to his contre
With moch glory and gret solempnite
And eke his yong suster Emelie
And thus with victory and melodye
Late I this this noble Duc to Athenes ride
And all his oost in armys him beside
And certes if it ner to long to hiere
I wold haue told fulli the manere
Hou was the regne of Femynye
By Theseus and be his chiualrie
And of the gret bataill for the nones
Bitwix Athenys and Amazones
And hou besegid was Ipolita
The faire hardi quene of Sithia
And of the feste that was at her wedding
And of tempest at her hom coming
But al that thing I must as now forbere
I haue god wot a large felde to ere
And weike ben the oxen in my plouȝ
The remenant of my tale is long I now
I nil nat leeten eke non of this route
Lat eueri felawe telle his tale aboute
And late se now who shal the souper winne
And there I lefte I will agein beginne
This Duke of whom I make mencioıı̄un
Whan he almost was cōmen to the toun
In all his wele and his most pride
He was war as he cast his yhe aside
Wher that ther kneled in the high wey
A company of Ladyes twey and twey
Ech aftir othir clad in clothes blake
